passages.2025-1: Maintaining an ecosystem just to conserve biodiversity will affect its commercial potential as well as the livelihoods dependent on the ecosystem. There is also a conflict between using an ecosystem only for livelihoods, for commercial exploitation, or strictly for conservation. Deforestation caused due to commercial exploitation will lead to indirect harm like floods, siltation problems and microclimatic instability, apart from adversely affecting livelihoods dependent on forests. These conflicts are particularly acute in developing countries where the dependence of people on the ecosystem is significant, and commercial exploitation has the potential to boost national income.
passages.2025-3: The history of renewable energy suggests there is a steep learning curve, meaning that, as more is produced, costs fall rapidly because of economies of scale and learning by doing. The firms’ green innovation is path-dependent: the more a firm does, the more it is likely to do in the future. The strongest evidence for this is the collapse in the price of solar energy, which became about 90% cheaper during the 2010s, repeatedly beating forecasts. Moving early and gradually gives economies more time to adjust, allowing them to reap the benefits of path-dependent green investment without much disruption. A late, more chaotic transition is costlier.
passages.2025-11: Each State in India faces a distinctive set of challenges regarding the impact of warming, but also offers its own set of opportunities for reducing emissions depending on its natural resources. For example, coastal States need to take action to protect their shores from sea level rise, districts that are drier need to prepare for variable monsoon precipitation. Himalayan regions have their own unique challenges, and selected parts of peninsular India and offshore areas offer great opportunities for harnessing wind power. These various aspects need to be considered for developing clear and sustainable goals for the future.
passages.2025-13: If the social inequality is the most acutely felt social problem in India, insecurity, more than poverty, is the most acutely felt economic problem. Besides those below the official poverty line, even those just over the poverty line are subject to multiple economic insecurities of various kinds (due to wealth and/or health risks, market fluctuations, job-related uncertainties). Many Government policies are actually intended towards mitigating these insecurities.
passages.2025-21: One of the dismal realities of the agricultural sector in independent India has been that it never experienced a high-growth phase, unlike the non-agricultural economy. The highest decadal growth (compound annual growth rate or CAGR) for agriculture has been just 3.5% in the 1980s. Also, after experiencing a spurt in decadal growth during the 1980s, agricultural growth suffered relative stagnation thereafter. This is in sharp contrast to non-agricultural growth, which consistently increased from the 1980s to 2000s.
passages.2025-23: In our country, handlooms are equated with a culture that ensures a continuity of tradition. This idea has become part of the public policy-framing and provides a legitimate basis for the State to support the sector. But the notion of tradition as a single, linear entity is being strongly contested today. The narratives dominant in defining culture/tradition in a particular way are seen to have emerged as the identities and histories of large sections. The discounted and, at times, forcibly stifled identities are fighting for their rightful place in history. Against this backdrop, when we promote handloom as a traditional industry, it is not surprising that large sections of our population choose to ignore it.
passages.2025-31: In our country, regrettably, teaching and learning for the examination have been our forte but the new demands of society and the future of work require critical and independent thinking, learning through doing, asking questions from multiple disciplinary perspectives on the same issue, using evidence for building arguments, and reflecting and articulation. Higher education should not “either be a mere servant of the government policy or a passive respondent to public mood.” Higher learning is all about how to think rather than what to think. Teaching has to be re-invented.
passages.2025-33: If there is inequality in the pattern of population growth, there is greater inequality in food production and utilization. As societies become wealthier, their consumption of animal products increases. This means that a greater proportion of such basic foodstuff as grains and legumes that could feed humans directly is instead being converted into feed for poultry and large farm animals. Yet this conversion of plant-based food into animal food for humans is far from efficient. Only 16% of the calories fed to chickens are recovered by us when we eat them. This conversion rate goes down to five to seven per cent in large animals that are fed grain to add fat and some protein before slaughter.
passages.2025-41: Over the next 30 years, many countries are promising to move to net-zero carbon, implying that household emissions will have to be cut to close to nothing. A leading climate scientist reckons that, at best, half the reduction might be achieved through demand-side measures, such as behavioural changes by individuals and households. And even that would require companies and governments to provide more incentives to change through supply-side investments to make low-carbon options cheaper and more widely available.
passages.2025-43: In only 50 years, the world’s consumption of raw materials has nearly quadrupled, to more than 100 billion tons. Less than 9% of this is reused. Batteries of old vehicles contain materials such as lithium, cobalt, manganese and nickel that are pricey and can be hard to obtain. Supply chains are long and complicated. Buyers’ risks are being aggravated by their suppliers’ poor environmental and labour standards. Reusing materials makes sense. Once batteries reach the ends of their lives, they should go back to a factory where their ingredients can be recovered and put into new batteries.
passages.2025-51: It is hard to predict how changes in the climate and the atmosphere’s chemistry will affect the prevalence and virulence of agricultural diseases. But there is a risk that such changes will make some plant infections more common in all climatic zones, perhaps catastrophically so. Part of the problem is that centuries of selective breeding have refined the genomes of most high-value crops. They are spectacular at growing in today’s conditions but genetic variations that are not immediately useful to them have been bred out. This is good for yields but bad for coping with changes. A minor disease or even an unknown one could suddenly rampage through a genetically honed crop.
passages.2025-53: “A good statesman, like any other sensible human being, learns more from his opponents than from his fervent supporters. For his supporters will push him to disaster unless his opponents show him where the dangers are. So if he is wise he will often pray to be delivered from his friends, because they will ruin him. But, though it hurts, he ought also to pray never to be left without opponents; for they keep him on the path of reason and good sense. The national unity of free people depends upon a sufficiently even balance of political power to make it impracticable for the administration to be arbitrary and for opposition to be revolutionary and irreconcilable.”
passages.2025-61: There has been no democracy that has grown economically without corporate capitalism. It helps in modernizing the economy and enabling the transition from rural to urban, and agriculture to industry and services, which are inevitable with growth. It generates jobs — and there is no other way to fix a country’s unemployment challenge without a further impetus to private business. Big companies can operate on a large scale and become competitive both domestically and externally. A vibrant corporate capitalist base also leads to additional revenues for the State — which in turn, can be used for greater welfare for the marginalized and creating a more level playing field in terms of opportunities.
passages.2025-63: “A network of voluntary associations stands as a ‘buffer’ between the relatively powerless individual and the potentially powerful State.”
passages.2025-71: A single number for inflation is an aggregate across different commodities and services — the price rise differs for different items of consumption. So, the single number is arrived at by assigning weights to different commodities and services. For WPI, the weights in production are used; for CPI, the consumption basket is used. But people are not homogeneous. The consumption basket is vastly different for the poor, the middle classes, and the rich. Hence, the CPI is different for each of these classes and a composite index requires averaging the baskets.
passages.2025-72: Trust stands commonly defined as being vulnerable to others. Entrepreneurship implies trust in others and willingness to expose oneself to betrayal. Trust in expert systems is the essence of globalizing behaviour; trust itself emerges as a super-commodity in the social market and defines the characteristics of goods and services in a global market. Trusting conduct also means holding others in good esteem, and an optimism that they are, or will be, competent in certain respects.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the author of the passage?
o: Conservation of biodiversity is not an issue to be worried about when some people depend on ecosystems for their livelihoods.
Commercial exploitation of forests goes against the fundamental rights of the people dependent on forests for food and shelter.
Sustenance of livelihood and degradation of ecosystem while being together exacerbate one another, leading to conflicts and imbalance.
Commercial exploitation of ecosystems should be completely stopped.
questions.e: The passage sets livelihoods, commercial use and conservation against one another and shows degradation hurting those who depend on the forest. Livelihood needs and degradation worsen each other — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q1

questions.q:
With reference to above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. No country needs to depend on ecosystems to boost national income.
II. Resource-rich countries need to share their resources with those of scant resources so as to prevent the degradation of ecosystems.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: The passage says commercial use of ecosystems can boost national income, contradicting I, and never discusses sharing resources between countries. Neither.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q2

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea of the passage?
o: Economies of scale is essential for transition to green growth.
Modern technological progress is intensely linked to path-dependent innovations.
Countries with large economies are in a better position to adopt green technologies.
Timing plays a crucial role in the case of green technology development.
questions.e: Green technology gets cheaper with scale, so an early, gradual move brings gains without disruption, while a late, chaotic one costs more. Timing is the central idea — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q3

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Path-dependent green investments will eventually most likely benefit growth as well as public finances in a country like India.
II. If other green technologies follow the same pattern as that of solar energy, there will most likely be an easy green transition.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Early green investment pays off with less disruption and cost (I), and solar's price collapse is the model for an easier transition (II). Both extend the author's reasoning.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q4

questions.q:
A natural number N is such that it can be expressed as N = p + q + r, where p, q and r are distinct factors of N.
How many numbers below 50 have this property?
questions.e: N = p + q + r with distinct divisors means 1 = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c with distinct whole numbers, whose only solution is 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6. So N is a multiple of 6: 8 such numbers below 50.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q5

questions.q: Three prime numbers p, q and r, each less than 20, are such that p − q = q − r. How many distinct possible values can we get for (p + q + r)?
questions.e: UPSC's key is (d). The primes need not be different (only the sums must be distinct), so p = q = r is allowed for each of the 8 primes below 20, giving more than 6 sums.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q6

questions.q: How many possible values of (p + q + r) are there satisfying 1/p + 1/q + 1/r = 1, where p, q and r are natural numbers (not necessarily distinct)?
questions.e: Unordered solutions of 1/p + 1/q + 1/r = 1: (3,3,3), (2,4,4), (2,3,6), with sums 9, 10, 11 — three values.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q7

questions.q: What comes at X and Y respectively in the following sequence? January, January, December, October, X, March, October, Y, September
questions.e: Forward gaps between months shrink by one: 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5. Nine months after October is July (X); six months after October is April (Y).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q8

questions.q: Team X scored a total of N runs in 20 overs. Team Y tied the score in 10% less overs. Had team Y’s average run rate (runs per over) been 50% higher, the scores would have been tied in 12 overs. How many runs were scored by team X?
questions.e: Y's rate is N/18; 1.5 times that is N/12, which reaches N in 12 overs for any N. The second condition adds nothing, so N cannot be found.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q9

questions.q: The price (p) of a commodity is first increased by k%; then decreased by k%; again increased by k%; and again decreased by k%. If the new price is q, then what is the relation between p and q?
questions.e: A k% rise then a k% fall multiplies by (100 + k)(100 − k)/10⁴ = (10⁴ − k²)/10⁴. Twice over: q = p(10⁴ − k²)²/10⁸, i.e. p(10⁴ − k²)² = q × 10⁸.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q10

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and pragmatic message conveyed by the author of the passage?
o: The mitigation and adaptation strategies to address/tackle the climate change is essentially the responsibility of each State.
India is too diverse to implement any effective strategy or programme to address/tackle the climate change.
It is basically the responsibility of the Union Government to implement the climate action plans and ensure net zero emissions.
India needs to formulate effective climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies at the State/region level.
questions.e: Impacts and opportunities differ from coasts to dry districts to the Himalaya, and these differences must shape goals. Strategies are needed at State or regional level — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q11

questions.q:
With reference to the passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Green energy production can be linked to/integrated with the climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies.
II. Effects of climate change are much more severe in coastal and mountainous regions.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Each State's resources, such as wind, are treated as chances to cut emissions within its climate response (I). Regional challenges are called distinctive, not more severe (II fails).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q12

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the passage?
o: India’s political executive should be aware that poverty and social inequality and the consequent sense of insecurity is the main social problem.
In India, poverty is the primary reason for social inequality and insecurity.
Poverty and social inequality are so intricately linked that they pose an unmanageable crisis for India.
Insecurity, more than poverty, is the main economic issue that Government policies must address.
questions.e: Insecurity, felt even just above the poverty line, is called a more acute economic problem than poverty, and many policies aim at it — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q13

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. People above the poverty line also are prone to suffer from anxiety about economic insecurity.
II. Eradication of poverty can result in peace and social equality in the country.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: The passage says even those just over the poverty line face economic insecurity (I). It never links ending poverty to peace or social equality.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q14

questions.q:
A solid cube is painted yellow on all its faces. The cube is then cut into 60 smaller but equal pieces by making the minimum number of cuts. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. The minimum number of cuts is 9.
II. The number of smaller pieces which are not painted on any face is 6.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: 60 = 3 × 4 × 5 needs 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 cuts. Unpainted inner pieces: 1 × 2 × 3 = 6. Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q15

questions.q: If 7 * 24 = 25 and 12 * 16 = 20, then what is 16 * 63 equal to?
questions.e: 7, 24, 25 and 12, 16, 20 are Pythagorean triples, so a * b = √(a² + b²). 16 * 63 = √(256 + 3969) = 65.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q16

questions.q: The petrol price shot up by 10% as a result of the hike in crude oil prices. The price of petrol before the hike was ₹90 per litre. A person travels 2200 km every month and his car gives a mileage of 16 km per litre. By how many km should he reduce his travel if he wants to maintain his expenditure at the previous level?
questions.e: With a fixed budget, distance falls in proportion to the price: 2200 × 100/110 = 2000 km. Reduce by 200 km.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q17

questions.q: A 4-digit number N is such that when divided by 3, 5, 6, 9 leaves a remainder 1, 3, 4, 7 respectively. What is the smallest value of N?
questions.e: Each remainder is 2 less than the divisor, so N + 2 is a multiple of LCM 90. Smallest 4-digit: 1080 − 2 = 1078.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q18

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. If A ≤ B > C < D > E > F ≥ G = H; then B is always greater than E.
II. If P > Q = R ≥ S = T ≤ U = V > W; then S is always less than V.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A comparison is certain only if every sign between the letters points the same way. B and E are separated by a reversal at C, and S = T ≤ U = V allows S = V. Neither.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q19

questions.q: What is the unit digit in the multiplication of 1 × 3 × 5 × 7 × 9 × ... × 999?
questions.e: The product of odd numbers is odd and contains 5, so it ends in 5.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q20

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the corollary to the above passage?
o: The benefit of economic reforms percolates down more slowly to the agriculture sector than in other sectors of the economy.
For India, the green revolution was not as useful as it was expected to be.
India lagged behind other countries in adapting mechanized and modern farming.
Rural-to-urban migration resulted in the stagnant agriculture sector.
questions.e: Agriculture peaked at 3.5% growth in the 1980s and then stagnated, while non-farm growth kept rising. Reform gains reached agriculture more slowly — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q21

questions.q:
With reference to the passage, the following assumptions have been made: The growing divergence between the fortunes of the agricultural and non-agricultural economy in India could have been reduced/contained by:
I. adapting large-scale cultivation of commercial crops and viable corporate farming.
II. providing free insurance for all crops and heavily subsidizing seeds, fertilizers, electricity and farm machinery at par with developed countries.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: The passage only records the widening gap; it proposes no remedies. Both statements are policy prescriptions it does not make.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q22

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical and rational message conveyed by the author of the passage?
o: We need to free the handloom industry from the limited narrative linked to preserving cultural heritage.
Continued State support to the handloom industry ensures the preservation of some of our glorious art forms and old traditions.
Household units of the handloom sector should be modernized and made an economically viable organized industry.
Handloom products need to be converted to machine-made designer products so as to make them more popular.
questions.e: Tying handloom to one idea of tradition has backfired, as that idea is contested and many ignore handloom. Handloom should be freed from the narrow heritage narrative — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q23

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. There is no need for the State to be involved in any manner in the handloom sector.
II. Handloom products are no longer appealing and attractive in the rapidly changing modern world.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: The passage criticises the narrative used to promote handloom, not State involvement or the products. Neither.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q24

questions.q: Consider the first 100 natural numbers. How many of them are not divisible by any one of 2, 3, 5, 7 and 9?
questions.e: Numbers to 100 not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7 (9 is covered by 3): 1 and the 21 primes from 11 to 97: 22.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q25

questions.q: If 4 ≤ x ≤ 8 and 2 ≤ y ≤ 7, then what is the ratio of maximum value of (x + y) to minimum value of (x − y)?
questions.e: Max x + y = 15; min x − y = 4 − 7 = −3. Ratio −5, not listed: none of the above.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q26

questions.q: Let both p and k be prime numbers such that (p² + k) is also a prime number less than 30. What is the number of possible values of k?
questions.e: p and k cannot both be odd. p = 2: k = 3, 7, 13, 19 (sums 7, 11, 17, 23); k = 2 with p = 3 gives 11. Five values of k.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q27

questions.q:
There are n sets of numbers each having only three positive integers with LCM equal to 1001 and HCF equal to 1.
What is the value of n?
questions.e: Members are divisors of 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13 with LCM 1001 and HCF 1; there are well over 8 such sets.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q28

questions.q: Let PQR be a 3-digit number, PPT be a 3-digit number and PS be a 2-digit number, where P, Q, R, S, T are distinct non-zero digits. Further, PQR − PS = PPT. If Q = 3 and T < 6, then what is the number of possible values of (R, S)?
questions.e: Place values give 30 + R − S − T = 20P, forcing P = 1 and S + T = R + 10. With distinct digits, Q = 3 and T < 6: (R, S) = (2, 8), (2, 7), (4, 9). Three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q29

questions.q: Consider the sequence AB_CC_A_BCCC_BBC_C that follows a certain pattern. Which one of the following completes the sequence?
questions.e: The series is ABBCCC repeated three times; the blanks are B, C, B, A, C.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q30

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea conveyed by the passage?
o: India does not have enough resources for promoting quality education in its universities.
The institutions of higher learning in the country should not be under the control of the Government.
Classroom approach to higher education should be done away with.
Classroom needs to be reimagined and teaching needs to be re-invented.
questions.e: The author faults exam-focused teaching and calls for critical thinking and learning by doing, ending 'Teaching has to be re-invented' — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q31

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Higher education is a constantly evolving subject that needs to align towards new developments in all spheres of society.
II. In our country, sufficient funds are not allocated for promoting higher education.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Higher education must change as society's demands change (I). Funding is not discussed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q32

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the passage?
o: There is an urgent need for a public policy to promote the consumption of cereal-based foods in wealthier societies.
Animal-based food is far less efficient than grain/plant-based food in terms of production and utilization.
Plant-based protein should replace the animal-based protein in our daily diets.
Inequality in food production and consumption is inevitable in any fast changing society.
questions.e: Feeding grain to animals returns only a small share of its calories to us. Animal food is far less efficient than plant food — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q33

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. The food manufacturing and processing industries in every country should align their objectives and processes in accordance with the changing needs of the societies.
II. Wealthier societies tend to incur great loss of calories of food materials due to indirect utilization of their agricultural produce.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Wealthier societies eat more animal products, losing most grain calories in the process (II). Food industries are not discussed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q34

questions.q: What is the maximum value of n such that 7 × 343 × 385 × 1000 × 2401 × 77777 is divisible by 35ⁿ?
questions.e: 35ⁿ needs n fives and n sevens. The product has four 5s (385 and 1000) and many 7s, so n = 4.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q35

questions.q: What is X in the sequence 24, X, 12, 18, 36, 90?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q36

questions.q: P and Q walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in opposite directions. P walks at an average speed of 5 rounds per hour and Q walks at an average speed of 3 rounds per hour. How many times will they cross each other between 5:20 a.m. and 7:00 a.m.?
questions.e: Moving in opposite directions they meet 8 times an hour, i.e. every 7.5 minutes after 5:00. Between 5:20 and 7:00 (ends excluded) that is 13 meetings, per UPSC's key.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q37

questions.q: If P = +, Q = −, R = ×, S = ÷, then insert the proper notations between the successive numbers in the equation 60_15_3_20_4 = 20:
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q38

questions.q: A tram overtakes 2 persons X and Y walking at an average speed of 3 km/hr and 4 km/hr in the same direction and completely passes them in 8 seconds and 9 seconds respectively. What is the length of the tram?
questions.e: (v − 3) × 8 = (v − 4) × 9 gives v = 12 km/h. Relative to X: 9 km/h = 2.5 m/s × 8 s = 20 m.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q39

questions.q: If N² = 12345678987654321, then how many digits does the number N have?
questions.e: A 17-digit perfect square has a 9-digit root: 111111111² = 12345678987654321.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q40

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea conveyed by the passage?
o: Moving to net-zero carbon is possible only by the reduction in household emissions.
Low-carbon behaviour in people can be brought about by incentivising them.
Cheaper goods and services can be made available to people by using low-carbon technologies.
Manufacturing industries that use low-carbon technologies should be provided with subsidies.
questions.e: Household emissions must fall to near zero, and behaviour change needs companies and governments to make low-carbon options cheaper. Incentives drive low-carbon behaviour — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q41

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Supply-side investments in companies can result in low-carbon behaviour in people.
II. People are not capable of adapting low-carbon behaviour without the involvement of Government and Companies.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Supply-side investment making low-carbon options cheap is linked to behaviour change (I). The passage does not say people cannot change at all without government and companies.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q42

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and pragmatic message conveyed by the passage?
o: Green economy is not possible without reusing critical minerals.
Every sector of economy should adapt the reuse of material resources immediately.
Circular economy can be beneficial for sustainable growth.
Circular use of material resources is the only option for some industries for their survival.
questions.e: Raw material use is soaring and costly, and recovering battery materials for reuse is recommended. Circular use can support sustainable growth — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q43

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Automobile factories are examples of the circular economy.
II. Economic growth is compatible with circular use of mineral resources.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Recycling battery materials to meet fast-growing demand assumes growth and circular use can coexist (II). Car factories are not said to be circular already.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q44

questions.q: A set (X) of 20 pipes can fill 70% of a tank in 14 minutes. Another set (Y) of 10 pipes fills 3/8th of the tank in 6 minutes. A third set (Z) of 16 pipes can empty half of the tank in 20 minutes. If half of the pipes of set X are closed and only half of the pipes of set Y are open, and all pipes of the set (Z) are open, then how long will it take to fill 50% of the tank?
questions.e: Per pipe per minute: X fills 1/400, Y 1/160, Z empties 1/640. 10 X-pipes (1/40) and 16 Z-pipes (−1/40) cancel, leaving 5 Y-pipes = 1/32. Half the tank: 16 minutes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q45

questions.q: If n is a natural number, then what is the number of distinct remainders of (1ⁿ + 2ⁿ) when divided by 4?
questions.e: 1ⁿ = 1 and 2ⁿ is a multiple of 4 for n ≥ 2. Remainder 3 for n = 1, 1 otherwise: two remainders.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q46

questions.q: Let P = QQQ be a 3-digit number. What is the HCF of P and 481?
questions.e: QQQ = 111Q = 3 × 37 × Q and 481 = 13 × 37; 13 never divides 3Q, so HCF = 37.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q47

questions.q: What is the 489th digit in the number 123456789101112...?
questions.e: 1–99 use 189 digits; the next 300 digits are exactly 100 three-digit numbers, 100 to 199. The 489th digit is the last digit of 199: 9.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q48

questions.q:
A mobile phone has been stolen. There are 3 suspects P, Q and R. They were questioned knowing that only one of them is guilty. Their responses are as follows: P. I did not steal. Q stole it. Q. R did not steal. I did not steal. R. I did not steal. I do not know who did it.
Who stole the mobile phone?
questions.e: No rule says who tells the truth; even assuming innocents are truthful, both 'P stole' and 'Q stole' fit. Cannot be concluded.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q49

questions.q:
Three teams P, Q, R participated in a tournament in which the teams play with one another exactly once. A win fetches a team 2 points and a draw 1 point. A team gets no point for a loss. Each team scored exactly one goal in the tournament. The team P got 3 points, Q got 2 points and R got 1 point. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. The result of the match between P and Q is a draw with the score 0 – 0.
II. The number of goals scored by R against Q is 1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Points force P one win and one draw, R one draw and one loss, and Q two draws. P's single goal beat R 1–0, so P–Q was 0–0 and Q–R 1–1. Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q50

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea conveyed by the passage?
o: Global climate change adversely affects the productivity of crops.
Our total dependence on genetically honed crops entails possible food insecurity.
Our food security should not depend on agricultural productivity alone.
Genetically honed crops should be replaced with their wild varieties in our present cultivation practices.
questions.e: Crops bred for high yields have lost the genetic variety to cope with change, and climate change may spread diseases. Total dependence on such crops risks food insecurity — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q51

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Global climate change can result in the migration of several plant diseases to new areas.
II. Scientific understanding of the wild relatives of our present crops would enable us to strengthen food security.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Changing climate may make infections more common in all zones, implying diseases can reach new areas (I). Wild relatives are not discussed, so II is not assumed. Answer keys for this item differ; (a) is taken here.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q52

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the author of the passage?
o: Without opposition parties, the administration in a democracy gets to become more responsible.
Democracy needs to have revolutionaries in opposition to keep the government alert.
Rulers in a democracy need the support of opposition for their political survival.
In a democracy, the opposition is indispensable for the balance of political power and good governance.
questions.e: A wise leader learns more from opponents, and free societies need a balance of political power. Opposition is indispensable for that balance and good governance — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q53

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. In a democracy, a strong opposition is required only if the Head of Government is indifferent.
II. The more aggressive the opposition, the better is the governance in a democracy.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Opposition is valued at all times, but not a revolutionary one. I adds a condition and II praises aggression the author warns against. Neither.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q54

questions.q:
P is the brother of Q and R. S is R’s mother. T is P’s father. How many of the following statements are definitely true?
I. S and T are a couple.
II. Q is T’s son.
III. T is Q’s father.
IV. S is P’s mother.
V. R is T’s daughter.
VI. P is S’s son.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: As siblings, P, Q, R have mother S and father T, so I, III, IV and VI hold. Q's and R's genders are unknown, so II and V are not definite. Four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q55

questions.q: If NO is coded as 210, NOT is coded as 4200 and NOTE is coded as 21000, then how is NOTES coded?
questions.e: The code is the product of letter positions: 14 × 15 = 210, × 20 = 4200, × 5 = 21000, × 19 = 399000.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q56

questions.q: If FRANCE is coded as 654321 and GERMANY is coded as 9158437, then how is YEMEN coded?
questions.e: From the two words: Y = 7, E = 1, M = 8, N = 3. YEMEN = 71813.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q57

questions.q: The 5-digit number PQRST (all distinct digits) is such that T ≠ 0. P is thrice T. S is greater than Q by 4, while Q is greater than R by 3. How many such 5-digit numbers are possible?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q58

questions.q: X can complete one-third of a certain work in 6 days, Y can complete one-third of the same work in 8 days and Z can complete three-fourth of the same work in 12 days. All of them work together for n days and then X and Z quit and Y alone finishes the remaining work in 8 2/3 days. What is n equal to?
questions.e: As 144 units: X 8, Y 6, Z 9 per day. Y's 8⅔ days do 52, leaving 92 done together at 23 a day: n = 4.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q59

questions.q: What is X in the sequence 1, 3, 6, 11, 18, X, 42?
questions.e: Differences are primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13: X = 18 + 11 = 29, and 29 + 13 = 42.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q60

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the author of the passage?
o: Corporate capitalism is important for economic growth of a State and also for democracy.
Corporate capitalism is imperative for a modern State to achieve its political objectives.
No State can ensure its economic survival for long without the role of corporate capitalism.
Corporate capitalism and democracy have mutual dependence for their continued existence.
questions.e: No democracy has grown without corporate capitalism, which modernises, creates jobs and funds welfare. It matters for growth and for democracy — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q61

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
I. Corporate capitalism promotes the growth of labour force and provides more employment opportunities.
II. Poor and marginalized sections of population are benefited by corporate capitalism due to trickle-down effect.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: UPSC's key accepts both. Corporate capitalism creates jobs (I) and its revenues help the marginalised (II), so both are taken as assumptions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q62

questions.q: Which one of the following statements reflects the best explanation of the above passage?
o: It emphasizes the inability of the State to enforce its will in practice against the opposition of certain groups within it.
It is a cooperative organization for the promotion of the well-being and development of the personality of its members.
It takes individuals out of a state of isolation and gives them a chance to participate in the common endeavour.
It permits citizens to have a variety of loyalties and allegiance.
questions.e: Voluntary associations buffer the weak individual from the strong State by drawing isolated people into joint action — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q63

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. There exists a natural number which when increased by 50% can have its number of factors unchanged.
II. There exists a natural number which when increased by 150% can have its number of factors unchanged.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: 2 → 3 (50% more) and 2 → 5 (150% more): all are primes with two factors. Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q64

questions.q: There are 7 places A, B, C, D, E, F and G in a city connected by various roads AB, AC, CD, DE, BF, EG and FG. A is 6 km south of B. A is 10 km west of C. D is 5 km east of E. C is 6 km north of D. F is 9 km west of B. F is 12 km north of G. A person travels from D to F through these roads. What is the distance covered by the person?
questions.e: Plotting the places, both routes from D to F — via C, A, B (6 + 10 + 6 + 9) and via E, G (5 + 14 + 12) — are 31 km.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q65

questions.q: In a certain code if 64 is written as 343 and 216 is written as 729, then how is 512 written in that code?
questions.e: n³ is coded as (n + 3)³: 4³ → 7³, 6³ → 9³, so 8³ → 11³ = 1331.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q66

questions.q: What is the remainder when 9³ + 9⁴ + 9⁵ + 9⁶ + ... + 9¹⁰⁰ is divided by 6?
questions.e: Every power of 9 leaves 3 on division by 6; 98 terms give 294, a multiple of 6: remainder 0.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q67

questions.q:
A question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.
Question:
What is the smallest 1-digit number having exactly 4 distinct factors?
Statement I: 2 is one of the factors.
Statement II: 3 is one of the factors.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?
o: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered even without using any of the Statements.
questions.e: One-digit numbers with exactly four factors are 6 and 8, so the answer is 6 without either statement.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q68

questions.q:
A question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.
Question: Let P, Q, R, S be distinct non-zero digits. If PP × PQ = RRSS, where P ≤ 3 and Q ≤ 4, then what is Q equal to?
Statement I: R = 1.
Statement II: S = 2.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?
o: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered even without using any of the Statements.
questions.e: PP × PQ = RRSS means P × PQ = 100R + S ≥ 100; with P ≤ 3, Q ≤ 4 only 33 × 34 = 1122 works, so Q = 4 without the statements.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q69

questions.q:
A question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.
Question: How is Q related to P?
Statement I: P has two sisters, R and S.
Statement II: R’s father is the brother of Q.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?
o: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone.
The Question cannot be answered even using any of the Statements.
questions.e: Together the statements make Q a sibling of P's father, but Q's gender is unknown (uncle or aunt). Not answerable.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q70

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and crucial message conveyed by the passage?
o: We must use WPI exclusively in measuring price rise and CPI should be done away with.
The present calculation of inflation rate does not correctly measure price rise of individual item/commodity.
Inflation data under-presents services in the consumption basket.
Knowledge of inflation rate is not really of any use to anybody in the country.
questions.e: A single inflation figure averages goods and services whose prices rise differently, so it cannot show any one item's price rise — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q71

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the passage?
o: Trustworthiness cannot be expected in entrepreneurship.
Trustworthy people are the most vulnerable people.
No economic activity is possible without being exposed to betrayal.
Trust is important though it entails risk.
questions.e: Trust is essential to enterprise and markets yet means accepting vulnerability to betrayal. Trust matters despite its risk — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q72

questions.q:
A question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.
Question: In a football match, team P playing against Q was behind by 3 goals with 10 minutes remaining. Does team P win the match?
Statement I: Team P scored 4 goals in the last 10 minutes.
Statement II: Team Q scored a total of 4 goals in the match.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?
o: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone.
The Question cannot be answered even using any of the Statements.
questions.e: Even together: if Q had 3 goals with 10 minutes left, it ends 4–4; if Q already had 4, P wins 5–4. Not answerable.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q73

questions.q:
A question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.
Question: Is (p + q)² − 4pq, where p, q are natural numbers, positive?
Statement I: p < q.
Statement II: p > q.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?
o: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone.
The Question can be answered even without using any of the Statements.
questions.e: (p + q)² − 4pq = (p − q)², positive unless p = q. Either statement rules out p = q.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q74

questions.q:
In a T20 cricket match, three players X, Y and Z scored a total of 37 runs. The ratio of number of runs scored by X to the number of runs scored by Y is equal to ratio of number of runs scored by Y to number of runs scored by Z.
Value-I: Runs scored by X
Value-II: Runs scored by Y
Value-III: Runs scored by Z
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
questions.e: X, Y, Z are in geometric progression summing to 37: 16, 12, 9 or 9, 12, 16 give opposite orders. Cannot be determined.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q75

questions.q:
Let p + q = 10, where p, q are integers.
Value-I: Maximum value of p × q when p, q are positive integers.
Value-II: Maximum value of p × q when p ≥ −6, q ≥ −4.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
questions.e: With sum 10 the product peaks at 5 × 5 = 25 in both cases; negative values only lower it. Equal.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q76

questions.q:
Consider a set of 11 numbers:
Value-I: Minimum value of the average of the numbers of the set when they are consecutive integers ≥ −5.
Value-II: Minimum value of the product of the numbers of the set when they are consecutive non-negative integers.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
questions.e: −5 to 5 averages 0; 0 × 1 × … × 10 = 0. Both are 0.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q77

questions.q:
The average of three numbers p, q and r is k. p is as much more than the average as q is less than the average.
What is the value of r?
questions.e: p and q are equally far above and below k, so p + q = 2k and r = k.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q78

questions.q:
Let x be a real number between 0 and 1. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. x² > x³.
II. x > √x.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: For 0 < x < 1, higher powers are smaller and roots larger: x² > x³ is true, x > √x false.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q79

questions.q: The difference between any two natural numbers is 10. What can be said about the natural numbers which are divisible by 5 and lie between these two numbers?
o: There is only one such number.
There are only two such numbers.
There can be more than one such number.
questions.e: Nine numbers lie strictly between; they contain one multiple of 5 if both ends are multiples of 5 (5, 15), otherwise two (3, 13). More than one is possible — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2025, CSAT Paper II, Q80
